title: Explicit finite ideal-layer tensor complex
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal and n a natural number. Put B_0=A/I^1 and B_{n+1}=A/I^(n+2). Define L_n=I^(n+1)/((I^1) I^(n+1)) as a B_0-module. Identify its carrier with the kernel of B_{n+1} to A/I^(n+1). Define the additive functor T_n from B_0-modules to B_{n+1}-modules as L_n tensor over B_0 followed by restriction along B_{n+1} to B_0, and define T_n(P) termwise on cochain complexes. For an adic datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], L_n is a finite type, finitely generated terms of P give finitely generated terms of T_n(P), and either strict support bound of P is inherited by T_n(P). These properties need no projectivity hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 094I, lemma-locally-constant-bounded, the displayed ideal-layer balancing identity; Tag 094H, lemma-locally-constant-tensor-product.

proof.text: Construct L_n as I^(n+1) modulo (I^1) times the whole I^(n+1)-module. Mathlib supplies its A/I^1-module action. The ideal-power quotient equivalence and factor_ker identify its carrier with the kernel of A/I^(n+2) to A/I^(n+1).

Take the ordinary tensor-left functor by L_n, followed by restriction of scalars along A/I^(n+2) to A/I. Both functors are additive, so applying them to the terms and differentials constructs the complex.

For the adic datum, the successor quotient is finite. The kernel identification makes L_n finite. Finitely generated terms over the finite residue ring and L_n have finite tensor product, hence finite successor-ring terms.
An additive functor sends a zero object to a zero object. Apply the strict-support characterizations to transport each support bound separately; no ordering of the two endpoints is used.
